findings.description: ConstrainedAnalysis inherits the public G1 solver, while its guard accepts a G2 owner during that solver's execution. Calling ElasticAnalysis.solve(owner, nodal), or the equivalent super-bound method, bypasses every G2 constraint equation and writes a G1-shaped accepted-history entry. This can commit a constraint-violating state and makes the resulting G2 checkpoint non-replayable. The frozen G2 contract explicitly prohibits exposing or using the inherited G1 zero-support solve on a G2 owner.
findings.gate: G2 constraint authority, accepted-state safety and authenticated restart
findings.observed: For a virgin straight one-element G2 owner with root affine x offset 0.001, ElasticAnalysis.solve(owner, zeros) returned success with u[0]=0, constraint norm 0.001, both generations advanced to 1, and a five-key G1 history entry. G2 resume rejected the emitted checkpoint with ValueError: G2 accepted-history schema. After a legitimate accepted prefix, the same unsupported route advanced both generations from 1 to 2 and again produced a non-replayable checkpoint.
findings.reproduction: Construct the registered straight ElasticElement and ConstraintSet, changing the first root affine row's offset to 0.001. For both virgin and legitimately accepted owners, call ElasticAnalysis.solve(owner, np.zeros(18)); inspect owner._constraint_trial, both generations and owner._accepted[-1]; serialize owner.checkpoint(); call ConstrainedAnalysis.resume with the checkpoint's actual SHA-256.
findings.required_change: Prevent the G1 solve entry point from operating on a G2 owner before evaluation or publication, while preserving the authorized G1 baseline. Add virgin and accepted-prefix regressions for both unbound-base and super-bound invocation, requiring rejection, unchanged committed bytes/generations/history, no active trial and continued checkpoint replay.
findings.title: Reject the inherited unconstrained G1 solve before it commits

findings.description: The S11 target-frame comparison and all three S14 covariance comparisons specify atol=1e-11 but omit rtol. The installed NumPy implementation defaults rtol to 1e-7, so these assertions can accept errors substantially larger than the frozen normalized invariant limit. In particular, approximately unit target-frame entries can differ by roughly 1e-7 and still pass. This is a verification defect, not evidence that the present numerical results actually exceed the required tolerance.
findings.gate: S11 physical target orientation and S14 covariance acceptance
findings.observed: Verified affected assertions at lines 146 and 232-234. Verified installed numpy/testing/_private/utils.py defines assert_allclose with rtol=1e-7 at line 1663 and documents atol + rtol * abs(desired) at line 1678.
findings.required_change: Enforce the registered dimensionless norm(a-b)/max(1,norm(a),norm(b)) <= 1e-11 criterion explicitly for every invariant comparison, including target rotations and covariance results. Do not rely on an implicit library tolerance.
findings.title: Enforce the frozen invariant tolerance in S11 and S14

findings.description: The frozen G2 contract explicitly requires target-frame prescribed work to be tested through the actual constraint Jacobian. The noncommuting-target test applies zero loads and checks continuation, replay and the final target rotation only. The only prescribed-work assertion in the entire G2 test module checks affine translation control_work_rate. No test establishes nonzero target-motion work, its sign, or the relationship between chart and spatial support moments.
findings.observed: Source inspection found no target-frame work comparison. The target-history solves at lines 142-144 use zero nodal loads; the sole control_work_rate assertion is the affine axial check at line 101.
findings.required_change: Add an independently derived nonzero prescribed-target virtual-work check using explicit target-frame perturbations and the actual constraint Jacobian. Verify the work sign and chart-to-spatial moment mapping at a nonzero, noncommuting rotation increment using every registered derivative step where numerical verification is used.
findings.title: Add the preregistered target-frame work verification

findings.description: The S14 contract includes constraint-row transport, but the covariance test checks only translations and spatial reaction forces/moments. It never evaluates transported constraint values, Jacobians or their work-dual row mapping, and never compares accepted physical rotations. Its single full identity-axis root orientation support also does not exercise selected-log-axis or relative-pose row transport. Passing this test therefore does not establish the stated G2 constraint covariance obligation.
findings.gate: S14 physical pose and constraint-row covariance
findings.observed: The complete comparison loop at lines 230-234 contains only translation, spatial-force and spatial-moment assertions. No constraint-row transport or accepted-rotation assertion follows it.
findings.required_change: Add independently specified DOF and constraint-row transport comparisons under proper global transformation, node-ID permutation and connectivity reversal. Include accepted physical rotations and the orientation/relative-pose semantics covered by the claimed G2 boundary, with explicit frozen normalization.
findings.title: Verify physical rotations and constraint-row transport in S14

scope.acceptance_boundary: Review of the private one/two-element exact-elastic G2 constraint implementation and its S09-S14 verification. All findings block proceeding to formal G2 confirmation. This review makes no general-static parity, G3, public integration, release or qualification claim.

scope.coverage_assessment: S09 provides meaningful exact affine-expansion and independent axial-equilibrium checks. S10-S12 analytically evaluate constraint derivatives and check all three registered finite-difference steps; the eccentric relative-pose unit fixture has nonzero chart coordinates and nonidentity relative frame. However, the assembled S12 tie is undeformed with axial offset and identity relative frame, while S13 compares a virgin, zero-multiplier system and leaves its returned constraint Hessians unused. These tests do not independently exercise a nonzero multiplier-curvature contribution in the assembled Newton system. This limitation is distinguished from the reproduced state-safety failure; no additional numerical mechanics defect is asserted from it.
scope.formal_confirmation: Not executed. The reproduced unsupported-route commit blocks formal confirmation regardless of finding severity; successor corrections and independent re-review are required.
scope.implementation_assessment: The normal G2 solve visibly forms the required multiplier residual and curvature tangent, uses committed-base shared rotations, checks rank before assembly, distinguishes chart and spatial reactions, and records target/control/multiplier history for replay. The corrected G1 post-callback and end-of-material-preparation authority guards are reused. These normal-path protections do not reject the inherited G1 solve route.
